name: Takaoka Daibutsu
description: The Takaoka Daibutsu is a monumental bronze Amida Buddha at Daibutsuji temple in Takaoka City, completed in 1933 after 26 years of casting using the city's renowned copper-work tradition. It is the tourism-standard holder of the third seat in Japan's Three Great Buddhas (Nihon Sandaibutsu) alongside Nara and Kamakura.
highlights: One of Japan's Three Great Buddhas
notes: Free to view; the statue is about 16 m tall. Takaoka has been a center of bronze casting since the early Edo period, and the Daibutsu is a celebrated product of that craft. About 20 min on foot or a short bus ride from Takaoka Station. Note: the third seat of 三大仏 has competing claimants (Gifu, Kobe); Takaoka is the widely used tourism convention.
